open_findings.summary: The F-HOOK-006 quote mask tracks quote state PER LINE, so a quoted string that spans newlines - a multi-line jq program, a heredoc - is seen as quoted on its first line and unquoted on the rest. Separators on later lines then split, and destructive-looking prose inside the quoted body can become a command word. Observed this session writing this very state file. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED: carrying quote state across the whole command, the obvious fix, converts a fail-safe nuisance into a fail-OPEN hole - one apostrophe in ordinary prose inside a heredoc ("don't") flips the state and masks every real separator after it, so a genuine trailing removal would no longer be judged. The correct repair is real shell tokenisation, which is a phase of its own and needs its own adversarial matrix. Workaround with no loss of protection: put a long quoted program in a file and pass it by path.

CLOSED by D-0536: authenticity now reaches the surfaces that start a model and gates the start (403 for an unattested descriptor, and for a caller that did not check at all). The blocker was the missing distinction between NO_SIGNATURE (a publisher placed a document and did not sign it) and SYNTHESISED (the product wrote the record from its own runtime, so there is nothing to verify) — the second is reported and NOT refused, which is what made the gate installable. Descriptor authenticity is shown on #/models in every lane, and it gates ACQUIRING. It does not gate STARTING an already-present model, and neither the CodeN model chooser (#/coden) nor /model in the terminal displays it — so a model whose publisher key was revoked after download can still be started, and the two shells show less than the catalogue page does. Not repaired here on purpose: the currently-running model is synthesised with no publisher and is therefore unsigned by construction, so gating activation on a verified descriptor would refuse to re-activate what the installation is already running. The fix is to distinguish >>unsigned because nobody signed it<< from >>unsigned because we synthesised it from the runtime<<, which is its own phase.
